answer: I would like to talk about someone much younger than me who really inspires me. A younger person I genuinely admire is my teenage cousin, who is remarkably mature for her age. She is my uncle's daughter and lives in Bogura, not far from us, so we see each other at family gatherings and during Eid. Despite being only sixteen, she has a level of [[determination]] that puts many adults to shame. As for what she has done, alongside her studies she has started a small online venture selling her own handmade crafts, such as embroidered bags and jewellery, which she runs entirely by herself. She takes the photos, manages the orders and even arranges the deliveries, all from her bedroom desk after school. What impresses me is how [[disciplined]] she is with her time, balancing school, hobbies and her little business without ever seeming stressed. She is also refreshingly [[self-aware]], knowing exactly what she wants and unafraid to pursue it. As for why I admire her, I think her generation faces a lot of pressure, yet she handles it with a calm confidence I did not have at her age. At sixteen, I was mainly worried about cricket scores and exam results, and I certainly could not have run a business. Watching her, I feel genuinely [[optimistic]] about the future. Honestly, she reminds me that age has little to do with wisdom or drive, and I sometimes catch myself learning from her rather than the other way around.

followUps.q: Do you think young people today are more mature than in the past?
followUps.answer: In some ways, yes. They have access to so much information and opportunity that many grow up faster. However, they also face more pressure, which can be quite [[overwhelming]] for some of them.

followUps.q: Would you like to start a small business like hers?
followUps.answer: Possibly, as a side project. With my business background it would be interesting, but at the moment my job keeps me very busy, and my priority is preparing to study abroad.
